title: A Wall That Took 2,000 Years: How the Great Wall Was Really Built
title_zh: 一道修了两千年的墙：长城究竟是怎么建成的
intro_zh: 本文约516词，讲述长城并非一道墙，而是不同诸侯国与王朝在两千多年里陆续修建的一系列防线：从战国的夯土墙，到秦始皇的连接与北扩，再到因地制宜的建筑材料、修墙人的组成、烽火传讯系统，以及明代砖石长城与今天的保护修复，信息密度较高的文化科普短篇。

paragraphs.en: Most visitors think the Great Wall is a single wall. It is not. It is a family of walls, built by different kingdoms and dynasties over more than two thousand years. The stone sections near Beijing that appear on every postcard are only the youngest and most famous part of a much longer story.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数游客以为长城只是一道墙。其实不是。它是一系列城墙，由不同的诸侯国与王朝在两千多年间陆续修建。今天出现在每张明信片上的北京附近石砌段落，只是这个漫长故事中年代最近、也最为人熟知的一部分。

paragraphs.en: The story starts around the 7th century BC, when small states in northern China began to construct walls of packed earth and stone to keep out horsemen from the steppe. These early walls were short and rough, sometimes only two or three metres high. Packed earth was cheap, and local people could repair it after each rainy season. Later the states of Qin, Zhao and Yan pushed their walls further north as they opened new farmland.
paragraphs.zh: 故事始于大约公元前7世纪，当时中国北方的小国开始用夯土和石块建造城墙，以阻挡来自草原的骑手。这些早期的墙又短又粗糙，有时只有两三米高。夯土便宜，当地人每个雨季过后都能自行修补。后来，秦、赵、燕三国向北开垦农田，也把城墙继续向北推。

paragraphs.en: In 221 BC the First Emperor of Qin united China. He ordered his generals to join the old walls into one long line and to push it north. Old records say some 300,000 soldiers and workers took part. The Qin wall ran for thousands of kilometres, mostly of pressed earth, and demanded an enormous amount of human labor. Guard posts stood at the main passes, and roads were built so that soldiers could move quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 公元前221年，秦始皇统一中国。他命令将领们把旧城墙连接成一条长线，并向北延伸。古书记载，大约三十万士兵和劳役参与其中。秦长城绵延数千公里，多为夯土筑成，耗费了巨量的人力。主要关隘设有哨所驻守，还修筑道路，以便士兵迅速调动。

paragraphs.en: Builders never used a single design. In the yellow-earth country of the middle reaches they pressed soil between wooden frames until it was hard as stone. In the western desert they laid reeds and gravel, layer upon layer, to resist the wind. In the mountains they cut local stone. Ming builders used bricks and a mortar made with sticky rice, and they carried nothing far if it could be found nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 建造者从不只用一种设计。在黄河中游的黄土地区，人们把土夹在木框之间夯实，直到硬如石头。在西部沙漠，他们一层层铺上芦苇和砾石来抵御风沙。在山区，他们开凿当地的石头。明代的工匠用砖，以及用糯米调制的灰浆；凡在附近能找到的材料，绝不从远处搬运。

paragraphs.en: Who built it? Soldiers in peacetime, farmers between harvests, and convicts sent north as punishment. Work was seasonal and often brutal. Many died, though the famous story of Lady Meng Jiang, whose tears are said to have brought a wall down, is legend rather than history. It still shows how heavy the memory of this work remains.
paragraphs.zh: 是谁修建的？和平时期的士兵、收割间隙的农民，以及被发配北方的刑徒。工程按季节进行，往往极其艰苦。许多人死在这里；至于孟姜女哭倒长城的故事，属于传说而非史实。但它仍说明，这段劳役的记忆有多么沉重。

paragraphs.en: The wall was never a simple barrier. A rider could not cross a well-guarded pass, but the real system was the signal towers: smoke by day, fire by night, so that a warning could travel hundreds of kilometres in hours. Behind the wall lay forts, supply towns and markets, and a single tower might hold a dozen men with food and arrows for a month. Goods and people still passed through the gates, with papers.
paragraphs.zh: 长城从来不是一道简单的屏障。骑手无法越过守卫严密的关隘，但真正的系统是烽火台：白天放烟，夜里举火，警报能在数小时内传递数百公里。城墙之后是堡垒、补给城镇和集市；一座烽火台可容纳十余人，备有够吃一个月的粮食和箭矢。货物与人员依旧凭文书从关口通行。

paragraphs.en: The wall we see today is mostly Ming work, from the 14th to the 17th century. Ming rulers faced strong nomad power to the north, so they rebuilt in brick and stone and added thousands of towers. A 2009 official survey measured every wall ever built at 21,196 kilometres, of which about 8,850 belong to the Ming.
paragraphs.zh: 今天我们看到的长城主要是明代工程，建于14至17世纪。明廷面对北方强大的游牧势力，因此用砖石重建，并增建了数千座敌楼。2009年的一项官方调查测得历代长城总长为21196公里，其中约8850公里属于明长城。

paragraphs.en: Today perhaps a third of the Ming wall has gone, worn away by wind and rain or lost to people taking bricks. Since 2006 a national law has protected it, and teams now restore damaged sections with traditional methods. At dawn, walkers still climb quiet ridges where the wall stretches like a stone river into the mountains.
paragraphs.zh: 如今明长城或许已有三分之一消失，被风雨侵蚀，或因人们取走砖石而损毁。自2006年起，一部国家法律对它加以保护，专业队伍也用传统方法修复受损段落。黎明时分，徒步者仍会爬上那些安静的山脊，看长城像一条石河，蜿蜒流入群山。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How the Great Wall was built and used over two thousand years.
Why foreign visitors are so attracted to the Great Wall.
How bricks and mortar were made in the Ming dynasty.
How the story of Lady Meng Jiang became famous.
questions.explain: 全文按时间顺序讲长城的修建：战国夯土墙、秦始皇连接北扩、因地制宜的材料、修墙者、烽火传讯系统、明代砖石长城与今日修复，因此主旨是长城两千多年间的建造与使用。B、C、D都只是文中一笔带过的细节或传说，不足以概括全文。

questions.q: According to the passage, what did the First Emperor of Qin do?
options: He was the first ruler to build walls in northern China.
He ordered the old walls to be joined into one line and extended north.
He moved his capital to the yellow-earth country.
He gave papers to merchants so they could pass the gates.
questions.explain: 第三段明确指出：秦始皇下令把旧城墙连接成一条长线，并向北延伸，还设有哨所与道路。A错，因为第二段说明公元前7世纪的小国早已开始筑墙；C、D在文中没有依据。

questions.q: Why did the builders use different materials in different places?
options: Because the government required a different style for each province.
Because they used whatever could be found near the building site.
Because stone was cheaper than earth everywhere in the north.
Because bricks were not invented until modern times.
questions.explain: 第四段列举三种做法：黄土区夯土、沙漠铺芦苇与砾石、山区凿石，并说凡附近能找到的材料绝不从远处搬运，可推断材料差异来自就地取材。A、C在文中没有依据，D与明代用砖的事实矛盾。

questions.q: In the last paragraph, the words 'has gone' most probably mean ______.
options: has been sold to other countries
questions.explain: 该句后紧跟“被风雨侵蚀，或因人们取砖而损毁”，可见has gone指“已经消失、损毁”，故选A。B、C与后文的修复和保护语境相反或无关，D在文中毫无依据。
